title: Record a controlled baseline before any probe
summary: Route-level rule: capture a control request whose only difference from the probe is the element under test, so every later signal can be attributed to that element rather than to dynamic content, caching or session drift.
preconditions: The tester is authorized to test the target.
The same request can be replayed without changing any other parameter.
verification_method: Replay the control request at least twice and confirm the response class is stable.
Send the probe and the control in the same session and compare status, body markers and timing.
Re-send both after the probe to confirm the target state did not change underneath the comparison.
known_failures: Dynamic content or per-request tokens make a byte-level diff meaningless.
A cache or CDN can serve a stale control response after the probe.
The endpoint mutates state, so the control is no longer a control once the probe runs.
steps: Select one observable that is stable across repeated control requests.
Record the control request and its response as the reference artifact.
Send the probe that differs only in the element under test.
Compare probe against control and note every attribute that moved.
Repeat in the reverse order to rule out ordering effects, then save both artifacts.

provenance.source_ref: NIST SP 800-115: Technical Guide to Information Security Testing and Assessment
provenance.notes: Human-drafted strategy summary grounded in the guide's test-planning and findings-analysis phases; not a verbatim quotation.

title: Escalate the injection channel instead of resending the same payload
summary: Route-level rule: once a parameter is confirmed to reach a query, move along a fixed channel ladder (visible error, union, boolean, time) and stop at the first channel that yields a stable controllable signal, instead of retrying payloads on a channel that has already failed.
preconditions: One parameter has been confirmed to reach a database query.
Repeated identical requests are possible within the testing budget.
verification_method: Confirm the chosen channel's signal disappears when the injected element is removed.
Confirm the signal returns when the element is restored in the same session.
Compare the channel's signal across at least three repeated requests before escalating or stopping.
known_failures: A generic error page hides parser errors while injection still works.
Escaping or type casting changes the boundary, so a payload that failed on a quoted parameter can succeed on a numeric one.
A timing channel becomes unusable when network jitter exceeds the injected delay.
A WAF can normalize the payload, making a channel look closed when it is only filtered.
steps: Record which channel is currently open and which has already failed.
If the error channel is open, capture the database-specific error text as evidence.
If errors are suppressed, switch to a boolean predicate and reuse the previously recorded observable.
If the response is too noisy for boolean comparison, switch to a time delay and measure it repeatedly.
Stop escalating once one channel yields a reproducible control, and record the channel with its evidence.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for SQL Injection; CWE-89
provenance.notes: Human-drafted strategy summary; the channel ladder paraphrases the testing guide's injection variants.

title: Diff an object and role matrix to find broken access control
summary: Route-level rule: enumerate a small matrix of object reference and acting role pairs, then diff the responses across rows that should not be equivalent, so a missing authorization check surfaces as an unexpected cross-row hit rather than as a guess.
preconditions: At least two accounts or roles can be used against the same endpoint.
Object references are enumerable or predictable enough to build a small matrix.
verification_method: Confirm the same request authorized as the owning role succeeds, as a control.
Confirm the same request made as a different role returns an equivalent object body rather than a denial.
Re-check the cross-role response after logging out and back in to rule out a cached session.
known_failures: A denial may be returned as a redirect to a login page, so status code alone is not the difference.
Identifiers may be indirect references that encode the owner, hiding the flaw.
Responses can be identical for unrelated reasons, so object content must be compared, not just status.
steps: List the object references to test and the roles that should be allowed to read each one.
Capture the authorized response for each cell of the matrix.
Replay each cell under a role that should be denied and record the response.
Compare body content and status across cells that differ only by role.
Escalate any cross-role success to a write or delete case before reporting impact.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Insecure Direct Object References; CWE-639
provenance.notes: Human-drafted strategy summary; the matrix framing paraphrases the testing guide's IDOR procedure.

title: Prove outbound control, then walk the reachability ladder
summary: Route-level rule: first prove the server performs a request whose destination the tester controls, then escalate that destination along a fixed ladder (loopback, private range, internal service, metadata endpoint) and stop at the first hop that returns a distinguishable response.
preconditions: The tester can supply a URL or host to the target.
A listener controlled by the tester is reachable from the target network.
verification_method: Confirm at least one request arrives at the tester-controlled listener.
Confirm the response body or timing changes when only the destination is altered.
Confirm the response differs from the baseline returned for a known unreachable destination.
known_failures: The fetcher may follow redirects only for allow-listed hosts, so a direct URL is rejected while a redirect is not.
DNS may resolve the same name differently inside and outside the target network.
A metadata endpoint may be reachable but require a specific header to return content.
Error text can reveal reachability that the response body deliberately hides.
steps: Supply a tester-controlled URL and confirm the inbound request in the listener log.
Confirm the target result reflects the listener's response, proving control over the fetched content.
Switch the destination to a loopback address and record whether the response class changes.
Walk the destination inward one hop at a time, keeping every other field identical.
Record the strongest reachable destination as evidence and stop escalating.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP WSTG v4.2: Testing for Server-Side Request Forgery; CWE-918
provenance.notes: Human-drafted strategy summary; the ladder framing paraphrases the testing guide's SSRF procedure.

title: Attack token integrity before guessing credentials
technique: Token integrity before credential brute force
summary: Route-level rule: when the target issues a structured token, spend the budget on the token's integrity check and claim handling first, because a weak verifier is a single deterministic step while credential guessing is a long, rate-limited search.
preconditions: The target issues a structured self-describing token.
A valid token can be obtained for at least one legitimate identity.
verification_method: Take a known-valid token, alter only the signed portion, and confirm the target rejects it, as a control.
Alter only the header or claim under suspicion and confirm the response differs from the control.
Re-send the accepted variant after re-authenticating to rule out a cached authorization decision.
known_failures: A token may be accepted but authorize nothing, so acceptance alone is not impact.
Key material may rotate, making a resigned token valid only for a short window.
The service may keep a server-side session that overrides the token claims.
Rejecting an unsigned token does not prove the verifier checks the signature correctly.
steps: Obtain one valid token and record its header, payload and signature as the control.
Establish control behaviour by sending a token with a single altered signature byte.
Change one header parameter at a time and record whether the token is still accepted.
Change one claim at a time, reusing the previously accepted encoding exactly.
Escalate the accepted variant to a concrete privilege change before reporting it.

provenance.notes: Human-drafted strategy summary grounded in the token structure and integrity requirements defined by the RFC.

title: Prove deserialization reachability before hunting a gadget chain
summary: Route-level rule: before spending effort on a gadget chain, prove that attacker-influenced bytes reach a deserializer and that the resulting object type is chosen by those bytes, because most targets fail at reachability rather than at chain construction.
preconditions: The target processes a serialized blob, cookie or message payload.
The tester can modify that blob and observe the target's response.
verification_method: Send a deliberately malformed blob and confirm the target reports a deserialization error rather than ignoring the field.
Confirm the error names the serialization format or library, proving the bytes are parsed.
Confirm a well-formed blob is processed normally after the malformed probe, ruling out a cached failure.
known_failures: The blob may be signed or encrypted, so modification fails before the deserializer is reached.
A class filter may deserialize the object but refuse the type a chain needs.
The deserializer may run in a context without the libraries the chain depends on.
A malformed probe can crash the worker and hide later, valid attempts.
steps: Capture a valid serialized blob and confirm it is accepted, as a control.
Modify one byte and confirm the target reports a parse or deserialization failure.
Record the error text as evidence that the bytes reach a deserializer.
Determine which type or class the blob selects and whether that choice is attacker-controlled.
Only after reachability is proven, evaluate candidate chains against the observed class filter.

provenance.source_ref: OWASP Top 10 2017 A8: Insecure Deserialization; CWE-502
provenance.notes: Human-drafted strategy summary; the reachability-first framing paraphrases the A8 guidance on attacker-controllable serialized data.
